nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Syzygium: From the Greek syzygos "coupled, joined", in reference to the paired branches and leaves.
- caryophyllatum: From the Greek caryon "nut" and phyllatum "leaves", for this tree resembling or associated with the clove plant.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Syzygium caryophyllatum is grey in colour and smooth. The branchlets are subterete and glabrous.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Syzygium caryophyllatum is grey in colour and smooth. 
The branchlets are subterete and glabrous.

seed.text: The seed of Syzygium caryophyllatum is enclosed in the flesh of the berry. It is about 0.5 cm across, light beige in colour. It is composed of 2 half green spheres, protected in a shell.
seed.text_html:
The seed of Syzygium caryophyllatum is enclosed in the flesh of the berry.
It is about 0.5 cm across, light beige in colour.
It is composed of 2 half green spheres, protected in a shell.

fruit.text: The fruits of Syzygium caryophyllatum are globose berries. The berry is crowned with the calyx lobes and it is glabrous. It is 0.5 cm across. The fruits are green, then pink and turn a deep purple or black colour at maturity. The fruits are edible.
fruit.text_html:
The fruits of Syzygium caryophyllatum are globose berries. 
The berry is crowned with the calyx lobes and it is glabrous. 
It is 0.5 cm across. 
The fruits are green, then pink and turn a deep purple or black colour at maturity. 
The fruits are edible.

flower.text: The inflorescences of Syzygium caryophyllatum are growing in terminal corymbose cymes. The flowers are bisexual. They are white in colour and 0.5 cm in size. The petals are calyptrate, with numerous stamens which bent inwards at the middle when in bud.
flower.text_html:
The inflorescences of Syzygium caryophyllatum are growing in terminal corymbose cymes. 
The flowers are bisexual. 
They are white in colour and 0.5 cm in size. 
The petals are calyptrate, with numerous stamens which bent inwards at the middle when in bud.

images.caption: Syzygium caryophyllatum flower with numerous stamens

leaf.text: The leaves of Syzygium caryophyllatum are simple, growing in an opposite and decussate arrangement. The petiole is less than 1cm long, canaliculate and glabrous. The leaves are 5 to 10 cm long and 1.5 to 4 cm wide. The leaf is obovate in shape, the apex is obtuse, the base is attenuate to acute and the margin is entire. There are many lateral nerves close, slender and prominent looped at the margin.
leaf.text_html:

The leaves are 5 to 10 cm long and 1.5 to 4 cm wide. 
The leaf is obovate in shape, the apex is obtuse, the base is attenuate to acute and the margin is entire. 
There are many lateral nerves close, slender and prominent looped at the margin.

habit.text: Syzygium caryophyllatum is a small evergreen tree, growing up to 6 m in height.
